>
> -removeDuplicateRecords
> logical. If there are several records of the same species at the same station (also

>
> So, it seems to me that the pdf instructions are incorrect, arent they?

# Yes, they are currently wrong in Version 2.2.0 on CRAN. It is fixed on GitHub. Thank you for pointing this out.

>
> And I would like to know:
> -confirmation if I should write (true or false) to get 1 line/ photo

# removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE

> -how to interpret the column "nimages" that appears in the generated csv. where does this value come from?

# I need to check (will do so by mid July, currently I don't have time). I think it is supposed to show how many images a row in the table represents, but need to confirm. I see the issue you mention when running example(recordTable) - when comparing rec_table3a and rec_table3b

> metadata <- recordTable(inDir                  = images,
>                         IDfrom                 = "directory",
>                         removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE)
> head(metadata)
> write.csv(metadata, file = "camtrapCOMPLET.csv" )

>                         IDfrom                 = "directory",
>                         minDeltaTime = 0,
>                         deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
>                         removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE)
> head(metadata)
> write.csv(metadata, file = "camtrapCOMPLET.csv" )

# if you tagged images in digiKam, use IDfrom = "metadata". minDeltaTime is 0 by default, so there is no need to state it explicitly. If minDeltaTime = 0, deltaTimeComparedTo does not change anything.

>
> But I am not sure what I am doing with the other possible (mandatory?) function arguments as I have these doubts:
>
>
> -camerasIndependent
> logical. If TRUE, species records are considered to be independent between cameras
> at a station.
> is it this one somehow affecting how the csv is created or is this for further analysis (occupancy models) etc? can I not include it in my code at all or if it is mandatory: what value should I write?

>

> to be considered independent (in minutes)

See this thread <https://groups.google.com/g/camtrapr/c/d8ceEoAqJoM/m/lTR2RGw6BgAJ> for an explanation of the different options with a few examples.

pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"
    if (!stationDir %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {

TO:

 pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"
   Albums$albumPath_full2 <- paste(Albums$label,Albums$relativePath,sep="")
  if (!stationDir0 %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {

And in 'addVideoHierarchicalSubject' I changed

metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(metadata.tmp.almostFullPath,
        digiKamVideoMetadata$almostFullPath)]

TO:

metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(digiKamVideoMetadata$name,
                                                                metadata.tmp.video$FileName)]

Not sure why the normal functions didn't find matches as the file paths looked very similar. But in any case, it works now.

Cheers,

Yannick

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I never tried renaming such a huge amount of images, so I have no hands-on experience with it. Also, I'm afrain the function was not optimized for speed either. You are also working on a server, right? To give us a rough idea, how many station directories and images do you wish to process?

Normally, you should see a message consisting of the station names and the number of images (try the example code in ?imageRename to see what I mean). Do you see these? And do you get any output (renamed images) at all? The answers would help narrow down what part of the function is slowing you down.

It may not be the actual renaming that takes so long, but rather the extraction of metadata (exiftool is called on each station folder in order to read date/time). Or it may have to do with the read/write times on the server (e.g. there are several calls to list.dirs and list.files).

Also, all stations are processed in sequence, not in parallel. That is certainly not ideal, but as Alex said, parallelization not help if the disk write speed is the bottleneck (especially if you are not working on an SSD). But maybe something goes wrong before that. Please let us know first if you get any output at all, then we take it from there.

Thank you,

Jürgen

The number of files was around 900000 images, divided in 4 station with each 15 cameras. I think the critical point is that since exiftool extracts the data from all the directory, it takes a lot to compute all the metadata.
One thing that could improve is if we split the calculation into different threads for each camera folder. This would improve exiftool performance and speed up the task. The problem I noticed is that photos are numbered based on the photos that have the same minute, so you must read all the files in the camera directory before doing all the calculation.

A secondary task that I had to do is to move the photos into different subfolders, based on the species tag the photos had on them. Using python and ThreadPoolExecutor I was able to rename the photos in about 3 hours of times. So this proves that using threads can yield better results.

I think it requires a good amount of work, so for now I will leave it as a suggestion. Even because I think it's rare that someone handles such amount of data.

Thanks for the reply,
Cheers
Bonat Laurence

Hi,

I'm glad it finished eventually. And it is quite an extreme case, both in the number of images and also 15 cameras per station (and hence hundreds of thousands of images per station) - so it is rather unusual.

I agree running exiftool on multiple threads would likely help, but then it would make sense to separate the parallelized Exiftool run from copying the files, which should not be parallelized. It would take me some time to implement. It is on the to do list already (https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/issues/16), but can't promise anything at this point. If you wish to get involved on GitHub, please feel free to DM me.

A long time ago (2015 or so) I experimented with the exiv2 library (instead of exiftool) and it seemed to be about 2x faster in extracting image metadata. But I haven't pursued that since, and installation seems complicated.

Moving photos into species folders automatically is not part of the standard workflow, so I think some custom code as you used is more suitable than adding to camtrapR. Side note, imageRename copies images and you moved them. So the performance benefits you saw may not be seen when copying.

Best,

Jürgen

p.S. Btw, I received the previous message, it was sent privately.

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] recodtable and removing duplicates
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the "n_images" column should have nothing to do with the removeDuplicateRecords argument. Instead, it tells you how many non-independent records (as defined by minDeltaTime) are represented by the record (a single row in the record table).

I just noticed however that with minDeltaTime = 0 it only works as intended when removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE (which is the default). If minDeltaime = 0 and removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE,  the values are wrong and it indeed looks as if it is counting. That is an artefact and not intended.

For now please use removeDuplicateRecords = T if you want to use the n_images column.
If minDeltaTime = 0, the current implementation will always return n_images = 1. Only with higher minDeltaTime you get values >1 in n_images. See the example below.

# all records (without duplicates) - n_images is correct
rec_table4a <- recordTable(inDir                  = wd_images_ID_species,

                           IDfrom                 = "directory",
                           minDeltaTime           = 0,

                           exclude                = "UNID",
                           timeZone               = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
                           removeDuplicateRecords = T
)

# all records (with duplicates) - n_images is wrong
rec_table4b <- recordTable(inDir                  = wd_images_ID_species,

                           IDfrom                 = "directory",
                           minDeltaTime           = 0,

                           exclude                = "UNID",
                           timeZone               = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
                           removeDuplicateRecords = F
)

# 60 minute independence (without duplicates) - n_images is correct
rec_table4c <- recordTable(inDir                  = wd_images_ID_species,
                           IDfrom                 = "directory",
                           minDeltaTime           = 60,
                           exclude                = "UNID",
                           timeZone               = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
                           deltaTimeComparedTo    = "lastRecord",
                           removeDuplicateRecords = T
)

# 60 minute independence (with duplicates) - not allowed; removeDuplicateRecords is set to TRUE automatically
rec_table4d <- recordTable(inDir                  = wd_images_ID_species,
                           IDfrom                 = "directory",
                           minDeltaTime           = 60,
                           exclude                = "UNID",
                           timeZone               = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
                           deltaTimeComparedTo    = "lastRecord",
                           removeDuplicateRecords = F        # not allowed
)

# rec_table4c and  rec_table4c  are identical
all.equal(rec_table4c, rec_table4d)
[1] TRUE

table(rec_table4a$n_images)

 1
55

table(rec_table4b$n_images)    # wrong

 1  2  3
55 10  2

table(rec_table4c$n_images)

 1  2  3
24 14  1

table(rec_table4d$n_images)

 1  2  3
24 14  1

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Nimble does not work
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

do you have NAs in your detection histories? I believe that is the issue. The models don't allow NAs / missing data in the detection histories, so the data structure differs a little from normal occupancy models in unmarked / ubms. Try replacing the NAs in the detection history with 0, and provide the effort matrix (which may contain NAs) as an observation covariate.

JAGS and Nimble don't allow NAs in the detection histories, hence the NAs must be introduced via the effort matrix as a observation covariate. The model will set the detection probability of all occasions with effort = NA to 0, thus ensuring that the 0s in the detection history doesn't bias detection probabilities.

The warning about the deterministic assignment can be ignored. It happens when the rOcc_v function is used to generate a new detection history (new.y), which is then compared to the actual detection history for calculating model residuals.

I will add the issue with NAs in the detection histories to the vignette.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Margarita,

if you want all records, use code 1 (removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE). The n_images column in that case is wrong, that is a bug. I'll fix it when I have the time.

As you noted, Code 2 removes duplicates and thus returns fewer images. This is intended. It is because two images of the same species in the same location in the same second usually do not provide any additional information. In your case it is different because of the custom n_individuals tags.

The n_images column is (currently) not designed to take duplicate images into account. It is for cases where minDeltaTime is greater than 0 (for example, 60 minutes). Then this column gives an indication how many non-independent images a given record represents. It is not intended for any analyses, but only to give the user an idea of how many records are lumped when setting minDeltaTime.

On that note, the function has two arguments for summarizing events by occasions (eventSummaryColumn, eventSummaryFunction). They is also intended for cases where minDeltaTime > 0. Summarizing is done after removing duplicates and thus would not help you. I may consider changing this, but would have to rethink a few things.

Best regards,

Jürgen
